properties.entry: generates a theme of the components, with a live preview

The themes of the components are CSS classes setting the custom properties --wicket-theme-*, which the style sheets of the components read. The pickers of the ThemeEditorPanel start from the theme chosen for the page in the top bar or in the drop-down above them; change a color and the components in the tabs below follow: progress bars, the JSON and the bean based tables, a collapsible panel, a floating panel, styled tabs and a modal dialog.

The text area holds the CSS class defining your theme; put it into your style sheet and the classes wicket-theme and yours on a page or a component, and the components inside take its colors. The changes are made in the browser through the CSS object model, so the page needs no inline style and works under a strict Content Security Policy.
Its title takes the theme's primary colors, like the headings of a table.
A window with a title bar, as the tables show their forms in.
The dialog follows the colors of the preview.
Collapsible panels inside each other, each opened and closed on its own.
The deepest panel, still in the theme's colors.
Closed at first; open it to see its text.
